stories.title: Taylor primed for Croker swansong to storybook career
stories.summary: Katie Taylor's storybook career is getting the crescendo she always wished for as she fights French challenger Flora Pili in Croke Park this evening. Years of megaphone diplomacy finally ended this summer when news filtered through that the Croker chiefs had softened on the idea of a boxing extravaganza on their turf and they were no longer quite so hung up on the 'security' concerns. Eddie Hearn and Peter McKenna had put their years of back-biting to one side - most of that coming from the former - in order to give Katie her dream farewell. The whole night is also testament to Croke Park's still sacred status in the national imagination. Even a soccer-playing woman from Bray - never the greatest stronghold for Gaelic games - is fixated with the gleaming palace on Jones's Road. Taylor said in her press conference in June that had she been offered Aviva Stadium as an alternative for her final fight, she'd have retired instead. As usual with a Taylor fight, there are a host of world title belts 'on the line' but still the night is being billed as 'Katie at Croker' rather than 'Taylor v Pili'.

stories.title: Joyce exit brings down curtain on colourful era
stories.summary: Padraic Joyce's departure brings to an end a colourful and tumultuous era in Galway football. A vibrant presence in the managerial paddock has exited stage left. Those pristine white runners will no longer traipse the inter-county sideline. The airpods have gone back in the case. The media will miss his occasionally unpredictable bluntness and his penchant for issuing cutting verdicts on his star players' performances. Rumours had swirled around social media in the week leading up to the All-Ireland final that Joyce was about to quit. On this desk, inquiries were made about whether we needed to have a 'Joyce departs...' article prepared and ready to go. Public denials were issued. There were, it has to be said, plenty of Galway supporters who wanted him gone in the wake of their sickening quarter-final defeat to Dublin. From our own sampling of the mood at the time, it's doubtful whether he would have survived a plebiscite within the county that week. But it appeared for all the world he was set on digging in and remaining at the helm. He was going to manage Galway to Sam or die trying.

stories.title: Irish sporting legends pay tribute to Katie Taylor
stories.summary: Some of Ireland's most successful and well-known sporting figures pay tribute to Katie Taylor as she signs off at Croke Park tonight. I have so, so much to say. Firstly, I want to say thank you. Thank you Katie for showing me what is possible. If you can’t see it, you can’t believe it and you allowed me to believe it. You allowed me to believe that with hard work, grace, humility, resilience and dedication, I too could become a phenomenal athlete. That’s exactly how you conducted yourself. You showed all the traits of excellence, which is why you are an icon. Growing up, I watched so many of your interviews, I got to get a scope of who you really are and I knew I wanted to be just like you. I finally got the opportunity to meet you in Texas after the Amanda Serrano fight last year. I was so nervous, but I was also so honoured. Even the fact that you willing to meet me after such a long night. You approached our interaction and conversation with so much grace and humility. You asked me questions and told jokes. It speaks to how much of an amazing person you are. Thank you so much for inspiring me, and the nation. You are a global icon. This is my petition to put you on the €1 coin because you are No 1 in my eyes. I wish you the very best tonight, and the very best in your next chapter. Katie Taylor is the greatest. She epitomises it in everything she does, her hard work and humility and resilience.

stories.title: Pat's v Bohs too close to call in FAI Cup quarter-final
stories.summary: Second and third place in the SSE Airtricity Men's Premier Division face off today in an exciting Club Orange FAI Cup quarter-final contest. Both teams have put up a fight to Shamrock Rovers, but with just a few games left, time may be running out for either team to win a miraculous league title. All eyes are on the cup. In the pick of the round, Bohemians make the short trip to Inchicore to face St Patrick's Athletic in Richmond Park, a trip that the Gypsies may have to get used to. Between the Bohs men’s and women’s teams there are seven games left in Dalymount Park in their respective leagues. The men also have a friendly against Bohemians Praha 1905, and their future is yet to be decided in the FAI Cup. After some farewell concerts, that will be it for the historic ground. Dalymount Park, as we know it, will be knocked down to make way for a brand new stadium. It was reported in June that Bohs were negotiating an agreement to play alongside their rivals Pat's for the next two seasons at least in Richmond Park.

stories.title: Refreshed Van der Flier ready for World Cup year
stories.summary: Leinster and Ireland flanker Josh van der Flier knows that nothing is won in early September, but that doesn't mean that the 2027 Rugby World Cup escapes the imagination ahead of the start of the 2026/27 season. Speaking at the launch of the IRFU’s new men’s and women’s national team jerseys at the Guinness Open Gate Brewery this week, the 33-year-old was in fine form, which could be attributed to a healthy body and mind. "(I’m) feeling fit as well and getting back into a bit of pre-season stuff and ready for a big few months." This optimistic outlook will come as soothing words to head coach Andy Farrell, who prepares his 12-month plan where all roads hopefully lead to a World Cup final in Sydney on Saturday, 13 November. Van der Flier was part of the two most recent touring squads to Japan in 2019 and France in 2023, where both Irish efforts were ended by the All Blacks. There is a feeling of now or never ahead of the next edition however, but van der Flier insists that he is taking the coming months one at a time. "It's always tempting to start thinking of those (major tournaments), but it's obviously like how rugby goes, it tends to be week-to-week and you've got to look after your pre-season first," he said.

stories.summary: Republic of Ireland international Troy Parrott made it a home debut to remember for Real Betis as he came off the bench to score the match-winning goal against La Liga giants Real Madrid. The Dubliner, who joined the Seville club from AZ Alkmaar last month, was the central figure as the hosts broke the deadlock in the 82nd minute at Estadio De La Cartujo. Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois made a fantastic save to deny Nelson Deossa's bullet of a header from a corner, but he could only parry it into the path of Parrott, who was quickest to react to fire home. "That's a striker's job," Parrott said after the match. "To go in after the ball and hope that it will fall in front of me. Look, in a game I might do this 10 times and it might not happen. So it's a mentality thing to just keep going in and hopefully it comes and today it did." It looked as if Jose Mourinho's side, who have begun the La Liga season with three straight wins, had rescued a point in the 87th minute when Carlos Espi found the back of the net with an acrobatic finish, but VAR deemed that Vinicius Junior had strayed offside. Los Blancos had another glorious chance to earn a share of the spoils but Killian Mbappe missed a penalty in added time.

stories.title: Kildare's Rattigan embracing football's new era
stories.summary: After playing a full season of inter-county football under the LGFA's new playing rule enhancements, Aoife Rattigan is enjoying doing the same with her club Cappagh as they work their way through the highly-competitive Kildare intermediate football championship. Having initially trialled them during the Lidl National Football League and the Higher Education colleges competitions, the LGFA fully approved 12 new rules for their games at a Special Congress in April of this year. Whereas six of these regulations mirror the changes brought into the men’s game – such as the two-point scoring arc, the 'three up’ rule and the ‘solo and go’ – the rest were focused more so on the current rules of the LGFA. Rattigan thoroughly enjoyed playing under these new rules for the Lilywhites and continued to embrace them by kicking no fewer than three two-pointers in Cappagh’s opening round intermediate group stage win at home to Confey on 11 August. Although Cappagh as a team weren't as familiar with the rule enhancements as those who had been operating on the inter-county scene, Rattigan believes her club colleagues have quickly come to terms with the way the game is now being played. "I loved playing the new rules all year with Kildare, but at the start it took us a while to get used to them," she said.

stories.title: Shearer was two hours from being Newcastle manager
stories.summary: Alan Shearer has revealed he was ditched as Newcastle manager in 2009 just two hours before he believed he was about to be unveiled as the club's permanent boss. The former striker said he had shaken hands on a three-year deal with then-owner Mike Ashley, two days after the club had been relegated from the Premier League following a 1-0 defeat to Aston Villa with Shearer in interim charge. Despite his failure to keep the club up, meetings with Ashley at the club’s training ground 48 hours later had been productive, with detailed plans made for the team’s upcoming season in the Championship. Speaking at a live show of the 'The Rest is Football’ podcast on London’s Southbank on Friday, Shearer revealed a member of Ashley’s entourage called to say the deal was off just two hours before it was set to be made public. "We got relegated on the Sunday against Aston Villa," he said. "Mike Ashley flew in to the training ground in his helicopter on the Tuesday and he was there all day. We were in a meeting for five, six, seven hours, going backwards and forwards. "We worked out the budget for what we had for the next 12 months, two years. The staff, contracts. And by three or four o’clock we stood up and we shook hands across the table – ‘That’s a deal – see you on Thursday to announce a three-year contract’. And I’ve never seen or spoken to him since.

stories.title: Hill's semi-final wait to continue after defeat to Jones
stories.summary: Aaron Hill's wait to reach a ranking event semi-final is set to go on after an agonising deciding frame defeat to Jak Jones in the British Open quarter-finals tonight. This was the fourth ranking event quarter-final of Hill's career, but it's now four defeats after his comeback fell short in a 5-4 loss. Jones, who inflicted one of those previous last eight defeats at the 2025 English Open, knocked in a break of 70 in the decider to send the Cork man out. Hill had led at 2-1 after back-to-back breaks of 63 and 67 but Jones then began to take control, winning the next three frames to leave himself on the brink of going through. The 24-year-old, who is at a career high of 38 in the world rankings, dug deep to win the next two, keeping his opponent scoreless, and knocking in his highest break of the match - a 78 - to force a dcider. And Hill got in first in the last frame but Jones did what he had to with the break of 70, finishing off the match with one final visit.

stories.summary: A quickfire brace from Alexander Isak ensured new Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola got off the mark at the third time of asking with a 2-0 win at Ipswich. The Reds had been held in the opening two matches of Iraola's reign to spark memories of his start to life at Bournemouth in 2023 where it took 10 matches before he could celebrate a maiden Premier League win. This defeat made it two in a row for Ipswich but, after they recovered from their nightmare start, Gary O’Neil’s team produced a spirited response and will aim to bounce back at Crystal Palace next week.

stories.summary: Shamrock Rovers opened a six-point gap at the top of the League of Ireland men's Premier Division table with just seven league games to be played, after a scoreless draw with Shelbourne in front of a crowd of 7251 at Tallaght Stadium. Rovers have stuttered of late, going out of the FAI Cup and Europe and they had to dig deep to get something off a Shels side that were difficult to break down The visitors defended well in numbers, relying on breakaway attacks to frustrate Stephen Bradley's side. Indeed, it was Shelbourne who created the better opportunities and John Russell’s side could well have taken all three points had keeper Ed McGinlty not brilliantly saved Odhran Casey’s 65th minute header which had goal written all over it. Before the game Rovers fans unveiled a banner in honour of the retired Rory Gaffney while former player and manager Liam Buckley was also honoured for his services to the club Both sides made changes from their most recent league games with Rovers captain Roberto Lopes back from suspension while he was partnered in a three-man defence by Lee Grace and former Irish international Enda Stevens who was an unused sub last week in Derry.

stories.title: Galway snatch unlikely victory in FAI Cup quarter-final
stories.summary: Galway United came from behind to snatch an unlikely victory over struggling Drogheda United and book their place in the semi-finals of the Club Orange Men's FAI Cup in the process. Lee Devitt's late strike – hitting the net via the inside of the post – won it for John Caulfield’s combative team who were fortunate to see Mark Doyle sent-off in the second for two bookable offences, the second a perceived case of simulation. At that point, it was the hosts who were in the ascendency at Sullivan & Lambe Park. After Brandon Kavanagh’s opener had been pegged back by Stephen Walsh in the first half, they were the ones who had stepped it up in pursuit of a lead goal. Prior to kick-off, home supporters unfurled a banner taking aim at owners Trivela, in which they implored the US-based owners to relinquish control of the club. Tensions have risen between sections of the supporter base and Trivela Group in recent months, while former chairperson Joanna Byrne - forced out by the club earlier this season - had previously acted as a conduit between the new owners and Drogheda’s ultra fan section. It was a notable first public display of discontent towards the owners from the fanbase since their takeover in late 2023.

So Alcaraz fixed his malfunctioning wardrobe by wearing a skin-tight vest underneath as he beat China’s Wu Yibing 6-3 6-4 6-1 in a two hours and 19 minutes. The 23-year-old, back to defend his title after four months out with a wrist injury, said he has surprised himself with how well he is playing. "I think today was a really high rhythm, the way he played was unbelievable," he said.

stories.title: Ferguson 'getting closer' to Brighton playing return
stories.summary: Republic of Ireland international Evan Ferguson is "getting closer" to a return to action after an enforced injury absence, according to Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler. The 21-year-old missed a significant portion of last season with an ankle injury, a setback which cut short his loan deal with Serie A club Roma, where he scored five goals in 22 games. Following ankle surgery in March however it has been a slow road to recovery for the striker. Brighton opened the season with a 4-0 win over Aston Villa before a 4-3 defeat at Chelsea last time out, with Ferguson still working his way back to fitness. It was thought that an early October appearance was a realistic target, but speaking ahead of Saturday’s Premier League visit of Leeds United, Hurzeler said there is no date set for his reintroduction. "He’s getting closer," he said. "He’s in his rehab. I can’t give a clear timescale for when he will be back.

stories.title: First Division wrap: Cork take the title after Bray draw
stories.summary: A first-half strike from Seán Maguire saw Cork City wrap up the First Division title and promotion to the top tier wth six games remaining following this 1-1 draw with Bray. Ajibola Oluwabiyi had put the home side in front early doors at the Carlisle Grounds but City gradually found their composure and sealed a deserved point and an immediate Premier Division return. Oluwabiyi had given Wanderers a well-earned lead to complement their positive start but Cork City will feel satisfied with how they responded to adversity and earned their title on the field. And UCD's failure to beat Cobh Ramblers at St Colman’s Park ensured the Students’ 20-point deficit is insurmountable with six games to play. A cagey start to the game saw both teams feel each other out, with a low effort from Ifunanyachi Achara the first shot in anger that was easily saved by Conor Brann in the City goal. stories.title: Sabalenka interrupts US Open match over smell of cannabis
stories.summary: World number one Aryna Sabalenka had an ⁠unusual interruption during her US Open third-round match on Friday, stopping play to alert the umpire to a strong smell of cannabis drifting onto Louis Armstrong Stadium. Sabalenka's pre-tournament form had raised plenty of concerns, but the top seed looked to have left her slump in the rear-view mirror as she did not face a single break point in her 6-3 6-4 victory over Uzbekistan's Kamilla Rakhimova. Her only issue during the morning session match was the smell of cannabis drifting into Louis Armstrong Stadium and she stopped play to alert the chair umpire. "Someone is smoking weed," the Belarusian said as she walked up to the chair umpire. While smoking is not allowed inside the US Open grounds, recreational cannabis is legal in New York and smoke from the surrounding Flushing Meadows-Corona Park can drift into the tennis venue. Jessica Pegula gave fellow former US Open runner-up Leylah Fernandez hope before coming back in style to seal a 1-6 6-4 6-3 win. The American third seed will next meet Sorana Cirstea.

stories.title: Dominant Waterford march into FAI Cup semi-finals
stories.summary: A dominant second-half performance from Waterford FC steered Graham Coughlan's side into their first Club Orange FAI Men's Cup semi-final since 2022 as they comfortably overcame Sligo Rovers in their quarter-final tie at the RSC. While it was far from vintage from the hosts during the opening 45 minutes, they still held the advantage thanks to Pádraig Amond's early breakthrough before second-half strikes from Tommy Lonergan and an unfortunate Ollie Denham own goal saw the Blues cruise into the final four. Waterford struck first after just eight minutes. Conan Noonan hooked the ball to the back post where Lonergan headed across goal for Amond, whose initial header was saved by Sam Sargeant. When the ball broke back to Evan McLaughlin, he slipped it into the path of Amond and the veteran forward applied a close-range right-footed finish to settle any early nerves among the home support. The home side nearly gifted Sligo an equaliser on 13 minutes when Benny Couto played the ball straight into the path of Luke Pearce. The striker raced clear on goal, but Stephen McMullan showed his quality by saving at the attacker's feet. After McLaughlin fired over from the edge of the penalty area, the visitors began to enjoy more possession and created a chance in the 39th minute. Seb Quirk collected a pass from Gareth McElroy before whipping in a teasing cross, but Archie Meekison failed to make contact.

stories.title: Taylor taking it all in ahead of Katie's final bout
stories.summary: Pete Taylor can remember times when he struggled to sell out tickets for people to see his daughter, Katie, box. Tomorrow evening, her professional career will come to a close at Croke Park in front of a packed house, with 80,000 looking on from inside the stadium. It's a phenomenal journey for a true pioneer of women's boxing, but Taylor senior also acknowledges that there's some sadness there, as his daughter's adventure at the elite level of the sport draws to a close. "We're all going to see the end of it. It's a legacy at the end of the day and yeah, it's going to be sad (but) I'm going to be happy that I don't have to sit through this again." Pete and Katie are on good terms now although things were different a decade ago, as the pair split in the build up to the Rio Olympics. It came as the result of Katie's parents separating but their journey to that point had brought Katie Olympic gold in London, four years previously.

stories.title: Dunne: Pioneer Taylor 'kicked that door down'
stories.summary: Former WBA super bantamweight world champion Bernard Dunne believes Katie Taylor's Croke Park fight has become an event of cultural significance that will leave a legacy for generations to come. Taylor brings the curtain down on a barrier-breaking career against French opponent Flora Pili in front of 80,000 fans in Dublin on Saturday night. "From an eight or nine-year-old kid trying to get involved in boxing, trying to get an opportunity to fight somebody, not even having that chance at that age to then go on and... I think it's five world titles, Olympic gold medal, six European titles, and then go on as a professional athlete and to achieve as much as she has. "In her last bout to have one of the biggest sporting events of the year in Croke Park - and if we're being honest with this, I know there's a lot of support but everybody's going to celebrate Katie Taylor's life really and her complete career." Dunne elaborated on the impact Taylor's career has had, not just on female boxers, but on the country as a whole. "It's nearly a cultural piece, you know, it's like it's an Irish identity piece that she's represented our country the way she has throughout the world," he added.

stories.title: Antvorskov leafrogs O'Brien ahead of decisive Rás weekend
stories.summary: The overall lead at the Rás na mBan changed for the third time in as many days on Friday, with the Danish rider Silje Antvorskov taking over at the top from stage 2 winner Aoife O'Brien of the Irish national team. O’Brien was distanced on the category one climb of Tickincor inside the final 32 kilometres of the stage to Carrick on Suir, with Cycling Ulster rider Aliyah Rafferty the strongest of the home competitors on that climb. She and Antvorskov were part of a five woman breakaway which was soon reduced to four, with these still together after the top of the short, steep Seskin Hill closer to the finish. The stage win was decided in a tense sprint to the line, with Antvorskov beating Frenchwoman Noemie Garnier, another Dane Olympia Norrid Mortensen and Rafferty to grab the win. "I tried driving it hard from the bottom to the top because I know that is the way I can climb the best," Antvorskov said of the climb of Tickinor. "And when we reached the top we were only four people. We worked together the rest of the race. Then I tried sprinting. It was flat and the wind was with me. It was possible." stories.title: London City kick off WSL season with victory over United
stories.summary: Former Barcelona captain Alexia Putellas celebrated her first Women's Super League victory as London City Lionesses beat Manchester United 2-1 at the Copperjax Community Stadium. New United boss Eva Olid did not have as jubilant an introduction to the English women’s top flight after the hosts dominated the first half and her side failed to register a shot on target before the break. United fell behind through Julia Zigiotti’s own goal in the ninth minute from a London City corner and nearly conceded another ahead of half-time before Danielle van de Donk doubled the hosts’ lead in the 82nd minute. They were denied a clean sheet, however, when Simi Awujo found the back of the net in second-half stoppage time. London City, who signed two-time Ballon d’Or winner Putellas in the summer, made history before a ball was kicked in Bromley when Eder Maestre named the first WSL opening day starting line-up without any English players. Initially the opener, from a London City corner, looked to have been headed home by Alanna Kennedy before it was confirmed Zigiotti had in fact nodded the ball past Phallon Tullis-Joyce.

stories.title: 'We're ahead of schedule' - Croke Park ready for Taylor
stories.summary: Having just dismantled the extravagant stage used for Bon Jovi's sellout concert last Sunday, Croke Park officials have been busy preparing for arguably the biggest night in Irish boxing history, as Katie Taylor gets ready to take on Flora Pili at GAA HQ. The stadium is well used to putting on huge shows, from Garth Brooks to Oasis. However it's a long time since it staged a card of boxing. It's 54 years since the last professional boxing event took place at Croke Park, when the great Muhammad Ali fought Al 'Blue' Lewis in July 1972. "It's very similar to what we do at concerts," he said. "It's in the middle of the park this time. I think the issues really were getting time to take down the whole Bon Jovi setup, putting in the boxing setup and then putting 12,000 seats onto the stadium ground. "We have two crews working really hard on it. Having seen it this morning, it looks like we're in great shape and ahead of schedule." It promises to be a unique atmosphere, with lots of families and children in attendance. Organisers have booked entertainment to cater for all tastes: Westlife are the headline act, with plenty of other spectacles planned.

stories.title: Leinster to return to Aviva for Munster clash in October
stories.summary: Leinster have confirmed their United Rugby Championship clash with Munster on the October Bank Holiday weekend will be played at Aviva Stadium. Leinster are going back to the RDS - now rebranded as Laya Arena - this season after the stadium's two-year redevelopment. They will play their first competitive game of the campaign there against Cardiff on 10 October. However the province will then make a quick return to Lansdowne Road, where they played most of their home matches last season. It's been confirmed the inter-pro derby against Munster will take place at the Aviva on Saturday, 24 October, 6pm kick-off. Last year the fixture took place at Croke Park, with Munster running out 31-14 winners in front of just under 52,000 fans.
